Interpretation of Probability

  • Examples:

    • “The chance of getting 1 when rolling a die is \(1/6 = 16.7\%\).”

    • Meaning: If we roll a die many times under the same conditions, we would get 1 roughly \(16.7\%\) of the time.

    • “The chance that a light bulb lasts longer than 2 years is \(72\%\).”

    • Meaning: If we turn on many light bulbs under the same conditions, about \(72\%\) of them would last longer than 2 years.

Axioms of Probability

  • The axioms of probability are properties that we intuitively expect a probability to have.

  • All probability theory is built on these axioms.

  • The mathematical foundations of probability, including these axioms, were laid out by Andrey Kolmogorov in 1933.
